stories.title: Pegula Saves Match Point to Stun Noskova, Eliminate Gauff from WTA Finals

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Gauff beat Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 on Thursday. Pegula also won. Gauff still went home. The head-to-head tiebreak was brutal. That's WTA Finals group-stage tennis. Pegula vs Andreeva on Saturday. #WTAFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
If you stayed up for Thursday night's WTA Finals action, you got your money's worth.

Jessica Pegula found herself serving with a match point against her — down in the third set against Linda Noskova — and somehow fought her way out. She went on to win 7-6(2), 4-6, 7-5 in 2 hours and 46 minutes. Sixteen aces. Noskova, the Wimbledon champion, hit 15 double faults. It was that kind of match.

The result knocked Coco Gauff out of the tournament. That is the brutal part of WTA Finals math: Gauff beat Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 on the same day, won her match, did everything right — and still got eliminated. Pegula's win over Noskova sealed Group 1 on the head-to-head tiebreak.

Noskova had already secured her semifinal spot at 2-0. She finished the round robin 2-1. Pegula advances as Group 1 runner-up and faces Mirra Andreeva in Saturday's first semifinal. The two have never played each other on tour before.

Meanwhile, Group 2 is still live. Aryna Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina are both 1-1, and they play today at noon PT. That match decides the last semifinal spot — and what happens in Sabalenka's year-end ranking picture.

Semis Saturday. Final Sunday. This WTA Finals has delivered.

Who wins Saturday — Andreeva or Pegula?

x_posts.text: Svitolina came back from a set down to beat Muchova earlier this week. Sabalenka got bageled in a set by Andreeva. Both are 1-1. Today's decider starts at noon PT. One advances to semis. #WTAFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The final WTA Finals semifinal spot is decided today.

Aryna Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina are both 1-1 in Group 2 after four days of round-robin play. The winner of their Friday afternoon match in Indian Wells joins Mirra Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, and Linda Noskova in Saturday's semifinals. The loser goes home.

For Sabalenka, the stakes go beyond just a semi spot. She entered this tournament ranked No. 2 in the world. After her 6-4, 6-0 loss to Andreeva on Wednesday, her year-end ranking is now in play. Andreeva, ranked No. 3, is already in the semis. The more ground Sabalenka loses, the closer that gap gets.

Svitolina came into this week in form. She beat Karolina Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 — a comeback from a set down in a match she could have lost. She has the resilience and the fight to give Sabalenka a serious test.

Match starts at noon PT in Indian Wells.

Who do you have — Sabalenka or Svitolina?

stories.title: ATP Finals Day 1 Schedule — Zverev Opens vs. Jodar; Fils Takes on Shelton in Night Session

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: ATP Finals Day 1 schedule (Sunday, Nov 15): Zverev vs Jodar at 2 PM CET. Fils vs Shelton at 8:30 PM CET. Alcaraz doesn't play until Monday vs Tiafoe. Turin is 2 days away. #ATPFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals is two days away, and the opening schedule is confirmed.

Sunday, November 15 at the Inalpi Arena in Turin opens with Alexander Zverev against Rafael Jodar not before 2:00 PM CET. The evening session, beginning at 8:30 PM CET, is Arthur Fils against Ben Shelton. Both matches are in the John McEnroe Group.

Carlos Alcaraz, the second seed and perhaps the tournament's biggest draw, does not play until Monday. He opens his Ivan Lendl Group campaign against Frances Tiafoe, also not before 2:00 PM CET on November 16.

A few things to note about Day 1. Zverev, who is trying to win a third ATP Finals title, opens against Jodar — the debutant who made history this season as the first player to qualify for the tournament in his debut year on the ATP Tour. Fils and Shelton are two of the most watchable young players in the game, and their McEnroe Group opener will likely be one of the loudest atmospheres of the week.

Turin runs through November 22. The draw keeps Zverev and Alcaraz apart until the semifinals at the earliest.

stories.title: WTA Finals Semifinals Set — Andreeva vs. Pegula Headlines a Saturday Showdown

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: WTA Finals semis are Saturday Nov 14 at noon PT. Andreeva vs Pegula is confirmed. Noskova's opponent is whoever wins Sabalenka-Svitolina today. The final is Sunday Nov 15. #WTAFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The WTA Finals semifinal picture is almost complete.

Group 1 is settled: Mirra Andreeva (Group 2 winner, 2-0) plays Jessica Pegula (Group 1 runner-up, 2-1) in Saturday's first semifinal. It is a first-ever WTA meeting between the two, which is rare at this stage of a season-ending event. Linda Noskova (Group 1 winner, 2-1) will face the winner of today's Sabalenka-Svitolina match.

Play starts at 12:00 PM PT on Saturday in Indian Wells. The final is Sunday, November 15.

Andreeva enters the semifinals having been the dominant player of this round robin. She went 2-0, beat both Svitolina and Sabalenka, and won both matches in straight sets. Pegula arrives having just survived the most dramatic match of the week — a match point against her, 16 aces, two and a half hours against the Wimbledon champion.

Noskova will find out her Saturday opponent sometime tonight after the Group 2 decider.

stories.title: ATP Finals Head-to-Head Preview — Zverev vs. Shelton and Alcaraz vs. Medvedev Are the Marquee Clashes

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: ATP Finals H2H preview: Zverev leads Shelton 4-0, with their last meeting the 2026 US Open final. Alcaraz vs Medvedev is a Grand Slam final rematch. Turin's group stage starts Sunday. #ATPFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals starts Sunday, and the head-to-head records between the eight players reveal a lot about where the drama will come from.

In the John McEnroe Group, the most revealing number is Zverev vs. Shelton: 4-0. The year-end No. 1 has never lost to the American, and their most recent match was the 2026 US Open final — a five-set battle Zverev won in a tiebreak. That is a significant head-to-head advantage going into their round-robin encounter. Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar are debutants who are talented enough to push Zverev, but the numbers favor the top seed to advance.

The Ivan Lendl Group is tighter. Alcaraz and Medvedev have played each other in Grand Slam finals — including the 2023 US Open — and there is no dominant H2H between the two. Alcaraz arrives with five titles this year and a 10-match winning streak. Medvedev has the indoor hard-court game and the experience of winning at this event before. Cobolli and Tiafoe are both first-timers with the weapons to disrupt the favorites.

Indoor hard courts in Turin favor big servers and aggressive players. That suits Shelton, Fils, and Tiafoe as much as it suits the top seeds.
